chunks: Yūnus, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “When the thief steals, his hand is cut off and he is made liable for what he took.”

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief, the one who steals
key_terms.غُرِّمَ: was made financially liable or required to pay compensation
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ: was cut off, referring here to the legal punishment
key_terms.مَا أَخَذَ: what he took, meaning the stolen property

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a thief in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling for theft: the thief is subject to the prescribed punishment of hand-cutting and must also compensate for the property taken. It highlights both the penal and financial consequences of theft in Islamic jurisprudence.
